main_text: A thematic node of the European Open Science Cloud EOSC Node | European Digital Twin Ocean Federating marine data, research environments, analytical services and computing resources for collaborative, FAIR and reproducible ocean science. Sign in with EOSC AAI Explore Resource Catalogue Explore Services Explore Research Environments This Node Landing Page is publicly accessible without login. Protected resources display an EOSC-AAI access route and their User Access Policy before users enter. Scope and users Resources Policies Governance Helpdesk View the dedicated Node page on eosc.eu → Acknowledgement The development and operation of the EOSC Node | European Digital Twin Ocean are supported by the EOSC-Marine project : Operationalizing the EOSC Node | European Digital Twin Ocean to Support the EU Mission Ocean & Waters . EOSC-Marine has received funding from the European Union’s Horizon Europe Research and Innovation Actions programme under grant agreement No 101292903, managed by the European Research Executive Agency (REA). Funded by the European Union. Views and opinions expressed are, however, those of the author(s) only and do not necessarily reflect those of the European Union or REA. Neither the European Union nor the granting authority can be held responsible for them. Node scope Marine data and digital environments for the European Digital Twin Ocean The Node connects multidisciplinary marine data with collaborative research environments, cloud computing, storage, analytical methods and FAIR research products. Originating from the Blue-Cloud initiative, it supports the construction, execution and sharing of ocean-science workflows across climate, biodiversity, ecosystem monitoring, coastal dynamics, fisheries, marine restoration, physical and biogeochemical oceanography, and offshore renewable energy. Users can discover datasets and services, work in Virtual Research Environments and Virtual Labs, run notebooks and analytical methods, manage shared files, publish research products and collaborate across organisations. Intended users Marine, climate, biodiversity and environmental researchers Research infrastructures and marine-data providers Ocean-observing and modelling communities Environmental agencies, coastal managers and policy stakeholders Data stewards, research software engineers and service providers Students, educators and Blue Economy innovators Node capabilities From discovery to reproducible analysis 1 Discover Search multidisciplinary data, research products, methods and services through Node catalogues. 2 Collaborate Work in community-oriented VREs with shared workspaces, communication and controlled membership. 3 Compute Use JupyterLab, RStudio, Galaxy and the Collaborative Computing Platform on managed backends. 4 Integrate Combine observations, models and data from European Blue Data Infrastructures. 5 Publish Create documented, citable and reusable data products with provenance and persistent records. 6 Reuse Adapt transparent workflows and services for new scientific questions and Digital Twin Ocean uses. Responsible organisation CNR – Consiglio Nazionale delle Ricerche CNR coordinates the Node and operates its D4Science-based digital infrastructure with European marine-data, research-infrastructure and technology partners. Access principle Public information, federated access Public pages and catalogues are available anonymously. Interactive resources use EOSC-compliant federated authentication; each resource below states whether access is open, moderated or restricted. Research resources Open environments for marine research Every entry provides its purpose and User Access Policy. The D4Science Access and Acceptable Use Policy applies to all D4Science-hosted environments; datasets and software may carry additional conditions shown in their records. Carbon–Plankton Dynamics Open EOSC AAI Model and explore nutrient, plankton, organic-matter and carbon dynamics, supporting investigation of biological carbon sequestration and marine ecosystem responses. UAP: Any EOSC user may authenticate and access the VLab; no consortium invitation is required. AUP: D4Science AUP and resource-specific data/software conditions. Resource information AUP Coastal Currents from Observations Open EOSC AAI Integrate HF-radar, drifter and satellite-altimetry observations to produce improved coastal surface-current maps and support transport or pollution studies. UAP: Any EOSC user may authenticate and access the VLab. AUP: D4Science AUP plus licences and attribution requirements of source observations. Resource information AUP EOSC Node EU DTO Lab Open EOSC AAI A general-purpose one-stop shop where researchers can discover and execute Node methods, use shared files, run notebooks or R analyses, and assemble workflows. UAP: Any EOSC user may authenticate and join the open Lab. AUP: D4Science AUP, fair-use quotas and method-specific conditions. Resource information AUP Ecosystem Workbench Open EOSC AAI Harmonise and analyse ecosystem-level Essential Ocean Variables and related observations to build quality-controlled, reusable marine ecosystem products. UAP: Any EOSC user may authenticate and access the Workbench. AUP: D4Science AUP and conditions attached to input and generated resources. Resource information AUP Eutrophication Workbench Open EOSC AAI Integrate and qualify chlorophyll, nutrient and oxygen observations for eutrophication assessment, climatologies and environmental indicators. UAP: Any EOSC user may authenticate and access the Workbench. AUP: D4Science AUP and provider conditions for data and analytical outputs. Resource information AUP Global Fisheries Atlas Open EOSC AAI Provide harmonised global fisheries and fish-stock knowledge through the Fisheries Atlas, Global Tuna Atlas, GRSF, semantic queries and reproducible R workflows. UAP: Any EOSC user may authenticate and access the VLab. AUP: D4Science AUP plus licences and citation requirements of fisheries records and products. Resource information AUP Integration of Coastal Ocean Observations along Europe Open EOSC AAI Combine European coastal observations for studies of transboundary transport and connectivity, extreme events and repeated ocean-glider sections. UAP: Any EOSC user may authenticate and access the ICOOE VLab. AUP: D4Science AUP and resource-specific data licences. Resource information AUP Marine Environmental Indicators Open EOSC AAI Compute and visualise Marine Heatwaves, Ocean Heat Content, TRIX and Storm Severity indicators for environmental assessment and decision support. UAP: Any EOSC user may authenticate and access the VLab. AUP: D4Science AUP and conditions attached to selected data products and algorithms. Resource information AUP Physics Workbench Open EOSC AAI Integrate, harmonise, quality-control and deduplicate in-situ temperature and salinity data for EOV products, reanalysis and data-driven applications. UAP: Any EOSC user may authenticate and access the Workbench. AUP: D4Science AUP and conditions of the contributing Blue Data Infrastructures. Resource information AUP Consortium and synergy environments Specialised collaboration spaces These environments are connected to the Node but may apply project- or community-specific membership rules. Their access model is stated before users follow the access link. EOSC-Marine Project VLab Restricted A collaborative environment for EOSC-Marine consortium members to share project documents and materials, communicate and coordinate project activities. UAP: Access is restricted to authorised EOSC-Marine project members and granted by invitation or manager approval after EOSC-AAI authentication. AUP: D4Science AUP, project confidentiality rules and resource-specific conditions. Request access through the resource index AUP Ecological Restoration Lab Open EOSC AAI Support marine-restoration planning, implementation and monitoring with guided protocol tools, spatial prioritisation, image analysis and regional digital-twin demonstrators. UAP: Public information and selected tools are anonymous; the complete environment and protected applications are available to authenticated EOSC users. AUP: D4Science AUP and conditions attached to each dataset, model and application. Resource information AUP MARINERG-i Moderated Support the development of an integrated European research infrastructure for offshore renewable-energy testing, shared knowledge, data-management procedures and community collaboration. UAP: EOSC users may request access; membership is reviewed by the VRE managers against the MARINERG-i community scope. AUP: D4Science AUP and MARINERG-i project or resource conditions. Request access through the resource index Project information AUP Access-status legend Public Available anonymously, although contribution functions may require authentication. Open EOSC AAI Any EOSC user may authenticate and join. Moderated An EOSC user submits a request reviewed by a VRE manager. Restricted Access is limited to an identified project or community. Node access and policies Clear conditions before access The public landing page, resource descriptions and catalogues can be consulted without login. Authentication is required only when a user enters a protected environment or invokes a protected service. EOSC AAI access Select Sign in with EOSC AAI , choose the academic or EOSC-compatible identity offered by the D4Science login service, authenticate with the identity provider, and return to the requested Node resource. Open the EOSC-compliant login → Acceptable Use Policy The policy covers authentication, VRE roles, open, moderated and private access models, permitted use, security, quotas, APIs and enforcement across D4Science-hosted Node resources. Read the Access and Acceptable Use Policy → User Access Policy Each resource card above states its access model. Authentication does not override membership rules: moderated access requires approval and restricted environments remain limited to authorised communities. View the live resource index → Resource conditions Source datasets, software and generated products retain their own licences, citation requirements and provider conditions. Users must consult the applicable catalogue record before reuse. Browse resource records → Privacy and data protection D4Science describes how personal data are processed, protected and retained when users access Gateway and VRE services. Read the privacy policy → EOSC Federation context The dedicated eosc.eu entry records the Node’s scope, capabilities, access points, status, coordination and participating organisations. Open the official Node entry → Governance Coordinated by CNR CNR – Consiglio Nazionale delle Ricerche is the coordinating organisation. CNR manages Node coordination, operations, security and infrastructure roles; MARIS provides technical coordination, and Trust-IT Services coordinates stakeholder engagement and dissemination. The Node is undertaken with European ocean and marine-data services, research infrastructures, e-infrastructures and scientific organisations: CNR MARIS Trust-IT IFREMER SSBE Mercator Ocean International VLIZ CMCC EMBL CINECA GRNET NUBISWARE FORTH IRD OGS HCMR EMSO-ERIC ETT University of Liège EGI INGV SOCIB EuroGOOS SMHI EMBRC-ERIC SIOS IEEE OceanScope PokaPok Node helpdesk How can we help? Contact the helpdesk for EOSC-AAI sign-in problems, resource-access requests, service incidents or questions about using Node environments. Include the resource name, page address, time of the issue and any error message. Open a Node helpdesk request For scientific or data-policy questions, use the contact information provided by the relevant resource or catalogue record. EOSC Node | European Digital Twin Ocean is coordinated by CNR and operated with European marine-data, research-infrastructure, e-infrastructure and scientific partners. Supported by the EU-funded EOSC-Marine project , grant agreement No 101292903. The digital environments are powered by D4Science . EOSC AAI sign-in Node page in EOSC Federation AUP Privacy Helpdesk

children.title: Access and Acceptable Use Policy | D4Science
children.main_text: Defines how users access the D4Science infrastructure, how Virtual Research Environments are governed, and which uses of services, APIs, and shared resources are permitted or prohibited. This is the final version 1.1 of the Access and Acceptable Use Policy, which entered into force on 1 April 2026. Purpose and Scope The D4Science infrastructure is a shared digital environment designed to support scientific research and innovation through collaborative access to data, computational resources, and services. As a common infrastructure operated for the benefit of multiple research communities, it is essential that access to its services is governed by clear rules ensuring secure and controlled use of infrastructure resources, protection of users and research activities, fair access to shared capabilities, and compliance with applicable legal and institutional requirements. This policy establishes the conditions under which users may access and use D4Science services. It applies to all interactions with the infrastructure, including access through Gateway portals, Virtual Research Environments (VREs), APIs, and programmatic interfaces. Relationship with the Policy Framework This policy is part of the D4Science Policy Framework and should be read together with the other policies governing the infrastructure. Together, these policies define the rules for access, usage, security, and data management, ensuring that the infrastructure operates as a secure, reliable, and sustainable environment supporting scientific research. Access to the Infrastructure Access to D4Science is provided through Gateway portals , which serve as the main entry point to infrastructure services. Through these portals, users can authenticate, discover available services, and participate in collaborative environments tailored to specific research communities. Access is governed by participation in Virtual Research Environments (VREs) , which define the scope of services and resources available to each user. User Roles The infrastructure supports a role-based access model that reflects the collaborative nature of research activities: Gateway Member: A registered user who can access the infrastructure and request participation in VREs. VRE Member: A user granted access to a specific VRE to use its services and resources. VRE Manager: Responsible for managing participation, approving requests, and defining community-specific access rules. Infrastructure Administrators: Responsible for operating and maintaining the core services. Authentication and Identity Management The D4Science infrastructure uses a robust Identity and Access Management (IAM) system. Authentication mechanisms include federated identities through eduGAIN , local accounts where permitted, and optional multi-factor authentication. Security Responsibility: Users are responsible for protecting their credentials and must not share access to their accounts. Virtual Research Environment Access Policies D4Science supports flexible access models to meet different community needs: • Open Access VRE: Allows any registered user to join without approval. • Moderated Access VRE: Requires a request reviewed by a VRE Manager. • Private Access VRE: Access is strictly by invitation only. These models enable the infrastructure to support both open and controlled scientific collaborations. Each VRE acts as a logical security context , ensuring that access to services and data is restricted to authorized users. Programmatic Access and APIs D4Science provides APIs to enable integration with external applications and automation of workflows. API access is based on OpenID Connect (OIDC) authentication and secure token-based authorization. To ensure fair use and system stability, the infrastructure may apply limits such as rate limits, quotas, and concurrency restrictions. Acceptable Use D4Science is a shared infrastructure supporting public research activities. Acceptable use includes scientific research, education, collaboration, and dissemination of results. Users must comply with applicable laws, respect intellectual property rights, and adhere to ethical standards. Prohibited Activities Certain activities are not permitted as they may compromise the infrastructure. Users must NOT : Bypass security mechanisms or access unauthorized data. Deploy malicious code or misuse APIs. Impersonate other users or perform illegal activities. These restrictions are necessary to protect the integrity of the infrastructure. Responsible Use of Resources D4Science is a shared resource and must be used responsibly. Users must avoid excessive consumption of storage, computational power, and API usage. Operational limits (quotas, constraints) may be enforced to ensure fair and sustainable use for all users. Reporting and Enforcement Users are encouraged to report any suspected security issues, including unauthorized access or abnormal behaviour, through the support portal. Failure to comply with this policy may result in suspension or termination of access, or removal from VREs. Policy Updates This policy may be updated to reflect changes in services, operational practices, or regulatory requirements. Updated versions will be published through official D4Science channels. Contact and Support For questions regarding the policy framework or infrastructure services, please visit our support portal: https://support.d4science.org © D4Science Infrastructure - ISTI-CNR, Pisa.

children.main_text: Terms of Use Defines the legal relationship between users and the D4Science infrastructure, including conditions of use, responsibilities, and limitations of liability. This is the final version 1.1 of the Terms of Use, which entered into force on 1 April 2026. Introduction These Terms of Use (“Terms”) define the conditions under which users may access and use the D4Science Infrastructure and the services provided through it. D4Science is a digital research infrastructure designed to support scientific communities by providing integrated environments where users can manage data, perform analyses, collaborate, and publish research results. These environments, known as Virtual Research Environments (VREs), enable distributed communities to work together using shared tools and resources. By accessing or using any component of the D4Science infrastructure, users acknowledge that they have read and understood these Terms and agree to comply with them. Users also acknowledge that the infrastructure operates within a broader governance framework composed of multiple policies, which collectively regulate its use. Purpose of the Infrastructure The D4Science infrastructure has been designed to support the full lifecycle of scientific research. It provides a set of integrated services that allow research communities to create, manage, analyse, and share knowledge in a collaborative digital environment. Through its Virtual Research Environments, D4Science enables: collaborative data analysis and interpretation management and sharing of research artefacts execution of computational workflows publication and discovery of research outputs The infrastructure promotes the principles of Open Science, encouraging transparency, reproducibility, and responsible sharing of scientific knowledge. Acknowledgement and Citation of D4Science D4Science is the result of sustained scientific and technological effort and is maintained as a shared research infrastructure. For this reason, users are strongly encouraged to acknowledge the use of the infrastructure in any scientific outputs produced with its support. Recommended citation M. Assante et al. Syst. 101: 555-563 https://doi.org/10.1016/j.future.2019.05.063 Additional guidance on how to cite D4Science, including references to specific services or Virtual Research Environments, is available at: https://www.d4science.org/how-cite Acknowledging the use of D4Science contributes to the visibility and sustainability of the infrastructure and supports its continued development. Faedo” (ISTI) located in Pisa, Italy. Definitions For clarity, the following terms are used throughout these Terms and the associated policy framework. D4Science Infrastructure: A distributed digital research infrastructure providing services, computing resources, and collaborative environments to scientific communities. Gateway: A web-based access point through which users authenticate and access infrastructure services. Virtual Research Environment (VRE): A customizable collaborative environment created for a specific research community or project. A VRE acts as a logical security context in which access to services and resources is controlled. Service: Any capability provided by the infrastructure, including data management, computational, collaboration, and API-based services. Research Artefact: Any digital resource used or produced within the infrastructure to support research activities, including datasets, models, workflows, software, scripts, notebooks, and applications. Scope of the Infrastructure The D4Science infrastructure provides a wide range of services supporting research activities, including data management, collaborative tools, computational platforms, and programmatic access through APIs. The infrastructure operates on a distributed model and may integrate resources hosted across: infrastructure managed by CNR infrastructure provided by GARR approved cloud providers As part of its evolution, the infrastructure periodically updates its services. For example, the DataMiner platform has been replaced by the Cloud Computing Platform (CCP), with legacy support planned until October 2026. Relationship with Other Policies These Terms are part of the D4Science Policy Framework, which includes several complementary documents addressing different aspects of infrastructure governance. Users typically access the infrastructure through a Gateway and may join one or more Virtual Research Environments, depending on their role and the policies defined by each community. Each VRE may define its own access rules and participation criteria. User Responsibilities Users play a key role in ensuring the proper use of the infrastructure. They are expected to use the services responsibly and in compliance with applicable laws and regulations. In particular, users must: ensure that they have the right to use and share any research artefacts they upload respect intellectual property and licensing conditions avoid actions that could compromise the security or stability of the infrastructure Responsibility: Users are responsible for maintaining the confidentiality of their credentials and for all activities performed through their accounts. Intellectual Property Users retain ownership of the research artefacts they upload, create, or manage within the infrastructure. By using the infrastructure, users grant the operator a non-exclusive licence to process such artefacts solely for the purpose of providing the services. The infrastructure operator does not claim ownership of user-generated content. Security and Monitoring The D4Science infrastructure implements security measures designed to protect its systems and users. These measures include authentication controls, monitoring of system activity, and logging of relevant events. Monitoring activities are carried out in accordance with applicable laws and institutional policies. The security framework of the infrastructure is aligned with recognized best practices and with the principles introduced by the NIS2 Directive. Service Availability The infrastructure operator makes reasonable efforts to ensure that services are available and reliable. However, services are provided on a best-effort basis, and availability may vary depending on operational conditions. Typical availability targets exceed 99.5%, although temporary interruptions may occur due to maintenance or unforeseen issues. Changes to Services D4Science evolves continuously to meet the needs of research communities and to adapt to technological and regulatory changes. Services may be updated, replaced, or discontinued over time. When possible, users will be informed in advance of significant changes affecting the services they use. Limitation of Liability The infrastructure is provided without guarantees regarding uninterrupted availability or the accuracy of results produced through its use. The operator is not responsible for: loss of data, service interruptions, inaccuracies in research artefacts, or results generated through computational services. Users remain responsible for validating their results. Termination of Access and Governing Law Access to the infrastructure may be suspended or terminated in cases such as: violation of applicable policies, security risks, misuse of services, or prolonged inactivity. Such measures are taken to protect the integrity of the infrastructure and its users. These Terms are governed by the laws of Italy. Policy Framework This document forms part of the D4Science Policy Framework .
